key_insight: Stacking ensemble learning delivered the most accurate predictions for UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness, while multitask neural networks offered strong shared-learning performance across the related welding targets.
engineering_relevance: These models can help optimize welding process settings by rapidly estimating key mechanical properties, supporting better joint quality and structural reliability.
method: Compared multitask neural network (MTNN) vs. stacking ensemble learning
Predicted three welding outputs: UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness
Evaluated model performance using RMSE and R²
evidence_signal: On the shared dataset, stacking achieved lower RMSE and higher R² across all three outputs, with particularly strong performance for UTS (RMSE 0.0263, R² 0.9863) and weld hardness (RMSE 0.0467, R² 0.9782).
watch_item: The best method may depend on whether the goal is highly task-specific accuracy or shared learning under limited data, so external validation is needed before deployment.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
